summary.en-US: Switch proxy profiles in one click. Keep page-visible location, timezone and WebRTC settings together, with clear identity diagnostics. For Firefox desktop.

version.approval_notes: Reviewer notes for the 1.1.4 listed release candidate are in docs/AMO-REVIEW.md in the source archive. The selected channel is listed; candidate preparation does not imply submission, signing or approval. manifest.json is authoritative for the submitted version. Firefox desktop minimum 140.0; no maximum. Schema 4 migrates versions 1–3, removes durable proxy usernames, and preserves the applied route independently of newer saved edits. Both proxy username and password live only in storage.session. Required authenticationInfo discloses existing credentials sent only to the user-selected proxy; required locationInfo and optional personallyIdentifyingInfo for direct GeoIP remain. Required-data update prompts may change. Fresh install makes no GeoIP request. Save changes stored configuration only; Apply changes runtime; blank credential fields keep the pair, either entered field replaces it, Clear removes the saved pair, and Duplicate copies no credentials. Terminal proxy lists prevent direct/system fallback. The blocking gate cancels ordinary non-bypassed extension-observable HTTP/HTTPS/WS/WSS and GeoIP requests when the applied route is unsafe or required session credentials are missing, even if the upstream also accepts anonymous clients. Firefox-protected browser-service requests cannot all be canceled: Firefox 158 Remote Settings could still attempt anonymous access to the selected proxy. Server-side rejection of anonymous access is required for browser-wide account identity; this extension is not a universal kill switch. Passive SOCKS health uses bounded request/generation/endpoint evidence, reports suspected trouble rather than proven outage, and applies bounded cooldown without HTTP replay, route changes or identity resets. Real Firefox tests include repeated flaps, outages, startup/restart, dual-mode authenticated/anonymous SOCKS credential-loss controls, HTTP/HTTPS/WS/WSS and proxy DNS with zero ordinary-fixture direct sentinel hits. The picker starts with an offline grid and makes no map request until Load online map is explicitly chosen for the current editor session. OpenFreeMap supplies HTTPS map data; viewed region and network-visible IP are disclosed to that provider/CDN. Direct/Off additionally requires optional personallyIdentifyingInfo consent. Provider bypasses and unsafe or credentialless required-auth routes deny map activation. The bounded background broker validates resources, rejects redirects, omits cookies/referrers/explicit proxy credentials and cancels stale sessions. MapLibre GL JS 6.11.2 is pinned and its renderer/CSS/worker/notices are bundled locally; the build verifies upstream source hashes and replaces the entire external worker-plugin loader with a denial stub. No remote executable code, RTL plugin or native GeolocateControl is enabled. CJK labels use brokered provider glyph data rather than OS fonts. Validated URL.href is shared by fetch and request correlation. A renderer FIFO bounds fanout to 8 active/256 waiting with a 60-second queue-inclusive deadline, no response-byte cache or retry, and cancellation on removal; aborted active work retains its slot until the RPC settles. Existing broker byte/network bounds are unchanged and glyph failures remain visible. Map rendering and no-WebGL fallback are separate release gates; manual coordinates remain usable on map failure. Existing stored credentials do not prove every HTTP proxy connection authenticated: a server accepting anonymous clients may never issue a 407 challenge. Require the proxy server to reject anonymous access for account identity. Final 1.1.4 candidate screenshots were captured from actual OpenFreeMap geography after the production rendering gate and independently reviewed; four image hashes and nine UI/renderer hashes match the production package. Capture uses an unsigned temporary add-on and is not signing or AMO approval. Historical tagged 1.1.3 screenshots and publication evidence remain unchanged. Listing-copy and media publishing is separate from version submission/finalization. The release remains draft until the exact listed AMO version is approved, the downloaded Mozilla-signed XPI matches its AMO hash and tagged payload, and permanent signature-enforcing stable Firefox installation passes. Historical listed 1.1.0/1.1.3 and unlisted 1.1.1/1.1.2 submissions and assets remain unchanged. No custom update URL; listed distribution uses Firefox’s default AMO update service, while GitHub itself does not update installations. See docs/PRIVACY.md.
